title: Archival Document Skeleton Standardization
business: A historical society digitizing paper records for public web access.
problem: Inconsistent document structures across digitized files prevent search engines from indexing content correctly, leading to poor discoverability.
solution: Implementing a standardized HTML document skeleton ensures that metadata, headers, and content sections are semantically defined, allowing crawlers to parse the archival records accurately.
steps: Define the root document structure using the standard HTML skeleton.
Insert metadata within the head element to describe the archival record.
Use semantic elements like header, article, and footer to organize the digitized text.
Apply links to connect related historical documents.
Validate the markup to ensure compliance with web standards.
outcome: Improved search engine visibility and consistent rendering of historical documents across all user devices.
limitation: HTML defines structure but not visual presentation; checking for visual consistency requires external CSS validation.
